questions.question: You are at a restaurant with a friend, and the bill is quite high. Your friend asks, 'What should we do?' Which of the following is the most polite way to suggest splitting the bill equally?
options: We can each pay for half.
Let's divide the cost.
How about we split it?
I think we should share the total.

questions.question: A colleague asks you for help with a project deadline, but you are already very busy. Which response is the most appropriate for politely refusing while offering an alternative?
options: I'm sorry, I can't do it right now. Maybe I can review your work later this week.
No, I don't have time for that.
I'm busy, so you should do it yourself.
That's a bad idea, but I'll help you anyway.
questions.answer: I'm sorry, I can't do it right now. Maybe I can review your work later this week.

questions.question: During a formal meeting, a senior manager makes a comment that you disagree with. Which response is the most professional and effective?
options: I completely agree with you.
That's not true at all.
I see your point, but I think there's another angle to consider.
You're wrong about that.
questions.answer: I see your point, but I think there's another angle to consider.

questions.question: You accidentally spill coffee on a guest's trousers. Which apology is the most sincere and appropriate?
options: I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to do that.
Oh no, I'm terribly sorry. I'll clean it up immediately.
Sorry about the mess. It was an accident.
I'm sorry, but I was in a hurry.
questions.answer: I'm terribly sorry. I'll clean it up immediately.

questions.question: A friend invites you to their party but you are not feeling well. Which response is the most polite way to decline?
options: I don't want to go.
I'm really sorry, but I'm not feeling well, so I won't be able to make it.
That sounds great, but I have to stay home.
I'm busy, so I can't come.
questions.answer: I'm really sorry, but I'm not feeling well, so I won't be able to make it.
